key_insight: VLMs still struggle with the overlooked first step of turning raw, heterogeneous medical folders into standardized image-text pairs, not just answering questions about prepared data.
clinical_relevance: In real clinical workflows, weak raw-data standardization could block downstream AI diagnosis by making diverse medical records and images hard to ingest reliably.
method: Built MDS-Bench to test raw medical data standardization from folder-level inputs.
Asked models to detect source formats, convert images into VLM-ready inputs, extract text, and assemble structured pairs.
Covers varied clinical settings, radiology modalities, annotation styles, and directory layouts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 1,939 manually annotated tasks, and the best model reported only a 48.6% end-to-end success rate.
watch_item: Results suggest current VLMs may be insufficient for deployment without robust preprocessing, format handling, and human oversight for messy real-world data.
paper_title: Solve the Missing First Step: Can VLMs Standardize Raw Heterogeneous Medical Data?
